#+title: Build and Cache

* Agreed Workflow
- Personal edits: test locally, commit as often as needed, then push the completed changes to =main=.
  One push starts one workflow for its latest commit, even when it contains several commits.
- Dependency automation: create an update PR with Nix's lock-file change log; approve its cache jobs,
  review the build results, then merge manually. Richer reports are planned. Merging starts a build
  of the final =main= commit.
- Same derivations reuse cached outputs. Different source snapshots or metadata can still require
  small generated outputs to be rebuilt; two workflow runs do not imply recompiling every package.
- Upgrade manually after the main-branch cache job completes. An urgent local input update or switch
  is always allowed; missing outputs can still build locally. Local builds are not automatically
  uploaded to Cachix.

* Current Implementation
[[file:workflows/build.yml][Build and cache]] runs on PRs targeting =main=, pushes to =main=, and manual dispatches.
Ordinary branch pushes do not trigger it. Fork PRs and manual runs on other branches are skipped.

| Runner       | Platform       | System outputs |
|--------------+----------------+----------------|
| ubuntu-24.04 | x86_64-linux   | az, echo, hws  |
| macos-15     | aarch64-darwin | rhayader       |

Linux targets share one Nix store. A failed build skips the explicit final upload for that job;
Cachix may already have uploaded successfully built dependencies. The other platform continues.
The final upload is a separate step: a successful build alone does not mean the cache is ready.
All Actions are pinned to commit SHAs.

** CI Cache Sources
| Cache                      | Purpose / evidence                                      |
|----------------------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| cache.nixos.org            | Default official Nixpkgs cache; retained by the installer |
| cache.numtide.com          | llm-agents' documented binary cache                      |
| cache.thalheim.io          | Declared by sops-nix's flake and used in its CI           |
| feel-co.cachix.org         | Public cache used by Hjem's documentation CI              |
| CACHIX_CACHE               | This repository's own outputs and runtime closures       |

Addresses and explicit keys were checked against the currently locked inputs; =feel-co='s public
key was also checked with the Cachix API. Cachix configures that cache and key through =extraPullNames=.
Hjem's documentation CI is evidence of upstream use, not a guarantee that our runtime outputs hit
that cache. =nix-index-database= downloads its pre-generated database from a pinned GitHub release;
it does not require adding =nix-community.cachix.org= for that download. No dedicated cache is added
for nix-darwin, and no unrelated CUDA, editor, or desktop caches are enabled.

The broad =nix-community= cache is intentionally omitted from CI; it is not synonymous with NUR.
An upstream cache hit depends on the exact output, platform, and dependencies. Missing outputs can
still build and enter the personal cache. Host cache settings are separate and unchanged here.

* GitHub Setup: Required Before Enabling Uploads
1. Create a Cachix cache and a write token scoped to that cache. Choose its visibility deliberately:
   anyone who can read the cache can inspect uploaded store contents, including generated configs.
   The official and community caches remain upstreams; this is not a mirror of all Nixpkgs.
2. In repository Settings -> Secrets and variables -> Actions -> Variables, set =CACHIX_CACHE= to
   the cache name (not its URL).
3. In Settings -> Environments, create both environments below *before* running the workflow.
   Put =CACHIX_AUTH_TOKEN= in each environment's secrets, not in repository or organization secrets.

| Environment    | Required protection                                     |
|----------------+---------------------------------------------------------|
| nix-cache-main | Selected branches/tags: allow only the branch =main=     |
| nix-cache-pr   | Required reviewers: yourself; review each candidate run |

For =nix-cache-pr=, leave "Prevent self-review" disabled so the sole maintainer can approve their
own runs. Restrict its allowed branches to =refs/pull/*/merge= if using selected-branch rules.
Approval permits the candidate code to run with the cache write credential: review workflow and
build-code changes before approving. Same-repository origin alone does not establish trust.

GitHub applies Environment protection before jobs start and releases secrets only after approval.
The workflow cannot configure those protections itself. Do not enable PR uploads if required
reviewers are unavailable on your repository's GitHub plan/visibility; agree on a different gate
first. Keep cache credentials out of repository/organization secrets so candidate workflows cannot
obtain them without the corresponding Environment gate. Do not use =pull_request_target= to build
candidate code with write credentials.

4. Commit and push the workflow when ready. Once it is on =main=, it can also be run through
   Actions -> Build and cache -> Run workflow, selecting =main=.
5. Check both platforms' build, final upload, and Cachix post-job steps. Fix failures and rerun the
   failed jobs as needed. No activation or deployment is performed by this workflow.

The Nix installer permits CI substitutions for =allowSubstitutes = false= derivations; local
substitution policy is unchanged. No production SOPS keys are needed. Only the committed snapshot
and its lock file are built; local uncommitted or untracked files are not sent to the runner.

* Dependency Update PRs
[[file:workflows/update.yml][Update flake inputs]] runs weekly on Sunday at 03:00 UTC (11:00 Asia/Shanghai), or manually on
=main=. Scheduled jobs can be delayed by GitHub. The updater performs no system builds and needs
no Cachix write credentials.

- Empty =inputs=: update all inputs.
- Space-separated input names, e.g. =llm-agents= or =hjem darwin=: request updates to those inputs.
  Input handling is delegated to the upstream Action and Nix. Indirect lock changes can still occur
  when an input's dependencies change or its references need reconciliation.
- Changed locks create or update a single PR from =automation/flake-update= to =main=. No lock
  difference means no new update PR is needed. The upstream action manages the branch lifecycle.
- Each run starts from the latest =main=; it does not accumulate pending updates from an earlier
  unmerged PR. Reserve the automation branch for the updater, not unrelated manual commits.
- The separate =FLAKE_UPDATE_TOKEN= repository secret must be a token restricted to this repository
  with Contents and Pull requests read/write permissions. Default =GITHUB_TOKEN= PR creation does
  not normally trigger another Actions workflow. No automatic merge or activation is configured.
- The first report contains Nix's input/revision/date change log. Package versions, upstream
  comparison links, and selected-module effects are still a separate reporting step.
- The PR body reserves =<!-- update-report:start -->= / =<!-- update-report:end -->= for the future
  report writer. These are placeholders only; no report generation or LLM call runs yet.

After committing and pushing both workflows, a manual update can be requested with:
#+begin_src sh
gh workflow run update.yml --repo hejsu/flakes --ref main
# Or update only llm-agents:
gh workflow run update.yml --repo hejsu/flakes --ref main -f inputs=llm-agents
#+end_src

Review and approve the resulting PR's =nix-cache-pr= jobs, then merge manually after reviewing the
results. The existing build workflow handles PR and post-merge caching. GitHub branch protection
is not configured here, so a failed job is visible but does not itself prohibit merging.

** Future Report Layer
Keep reporting separate from updating and caching. After both platform jobs finish, a separately
scoped report job should update the reserved PR-body block on success or failure, provided the
candidate commit is still current. It must not require builds to succeed before explaining a
failure. LLM/API failures should leave the raw checks and logs available, not block cache uploads.
An edit pushed to the PR branch automatically triggers another build; retrying an unchanged run is
mainly useful for transient infrastructure failures. None of this reporting is implemented yet.

* Next Steps
- [ ] Configure client substituters/public keys, including Determinate Nix's =nix.custom.conf=,
  and verify a real cache download. Uploading alone does not enable local consumption.
- [X] Add weekly/manual dependency-update PRs, with optional input selection such as =llm-agents=.
- [ ] Add input/package/selected-module change reports, using separately scoped reporting permissions.
- [ ] Measure cache storage and download performance, then choose retention for recent systems.

Homebrew, runtime container images/subscriptions, production state, automatic merges, automatic
activation, extra VM/integration tests, and a separate release branch are outside this first step.
